full.description: This is a photomicrograph of adrenal gland tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The image displays the distinct cellular architecture of the adrenal cortex, characterized by cords and nests of lipid-rich cells beneath a connective tissue capsule. Scattered among the cortical cells are intracellular eosinophilic inclusions commonly referred to as aldactone bodies. These histological findings are typically associated with aldosterone-producing adenomas or prolonged spironolactone administration.

random.description: This image is a photomicrograph of adrenal cortex tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows normal histological features of the adrenal gland, including cords of lipid-rich clear cells in the zona fasciculata alongside a fibrous capsule containing blood vessels and nerve bundles. There are no atypical cellular features, malignant changes, or architectural disruptions visible in this field. The appearance is consistent with normal adrenal cortex tissue rather than a neoplastic process or infection.
